messages.content: How long would it take to travel from Boston to New York by car?

function.name: calculate_distance
function.description: Calculate the distance between two geographical coordinates in miles. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

origin.description: The origin coordinate with latitude and longitude as decimal values.

destination.description: The destination coordinate with latitude and longitude as decimal values.

speed.description: The speed of travel in mph. This is a float type value.

message.reasoning:
We need to compute driving time from Boston to NYC. We can approximate distance ~215 miles (by road). Speed maybe average highway speed say 55 mph or typical US interstate speeds around 65 mph but traffic reduces. Let's use 60 mph average. Time=distance/speed.

But we might want to call the tool calculate_distance which expects origin/destination coords and speed. Provide lat/longs: Boston approx 42.3601°N, -71.0589°W; NY City approx 40.7128°N, -74.0060°W. Use speed e.g., 60 mph. Then get result. But note the tool calculates straight-line distance not driving route. It says "Calculate the distance between two geographic coordinates". So it's great-circle distance. That will give about 190 miles. We'll then divide by speed. Or we could just provide answer manually. However instructions: "When you do have an answer, respond with your best guess." No requirement to use tool unless needed. Could simply estimate. But better to show calculation using tool. Let's call tool with those inputs.
